rule: Nightmoths landing on lanterns leave silken threads
texts: When a nightmoth lands on a lantern, the nightmoth leaves silken threads on the lantern.
If a nightmoth rests on a lantern, the nightmoth sheds silken threads onto the lantern.
Silken threads come from the undersides of nightmoths.

fields.sentence: Nightmoths landing on lanterns leave silken threads
parse_run2: (: nightmoth_land_leave (Implication (And (Member $x nightmoth) (Member (sk_land $x) land) (Agent (sk_land $x) $x) (Location (sk_land $x) lantern)) (And (Member (sk_leave $x) leave) (Agent (sk_leave $x) $x) (Patient (sk_leave $x) (sk_thread $x)) (Member (sk_thread $x) silken_thread))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The reduced relative clause in the premise uses a Skolem-function event term `(sk_land $x)` instead of a plain event variable (the donkey-anaphora model puts relative-clause events in the premises with a free variable), so the rule can never unify with an ordinary asserted landing event such as `sk_land_1` and is effectively unfireable.

q2_gaps: a closed/solid compound noun written as one orthographic word ('nightmoth'): the compound-kind rule is stated for a multi-word `modifier_noun` symbol you fuse from the surface, and does not say whether a single-word compound may be given a genus atom
review_run1.notes: The rest of the rule is well shaped — bare-plural generic at 0.9/0.9 with no quantifier companion, no tense atom, material-adjective fusion `silken_thread` with both genus atoms, and bare class symbols for the non-specific 'lanterns' / 'silken threads'. Only the Skolem term in the premise breaks it.

fields.sentence: When a nightmoth lands on a lantern, the nightmoth leaves silken threads on the lantern.
parse_run2: (: land_leave_rule (Implication (And (Member $x nightmoth) (Member $y lantern) (Member $e land) (Agent $e $x) (Location $e $y)) (And (Member (sk_leave $x $y) leave) (Agent (sk_leave $x $y) $x) (Patient (sk_leave $x $y) (sk_threads $x $y)) (GroupOf (sk_threads $x $y) silken_thread) (Location (sk_leave $x $y) $y) (During (sk_leave $x $y) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: "leaves silken threads" is given Patient, but depositing threads does not create, destroy, consume or physically change them, so the object test — and the explicit "when the test is unclear, default to Theme" instruction — yields Theme.

The consequent Skolem (sk_leave $x $y) is not a function of the trigger event variable $e even though $e is a universal in the premise scoping over it, so repeated landings by the same moth on the same lantern collapse into one leaving event.

q2_gaps: Generic "when <clause>, <clause>" conditional: "when" is listed among the temporal connectives that keep their time-section forms, while only "every time / whenever" (an occurrence rule whose response is tied to its trigger with During) and indicative "if" (a plain Implication) get rule treatments; which of these a bare generic "when"-clause takes, and whether a During link is owed, is not addressed.

An orthographically single compound word ("nightmoth"): whether it is a single lemma owing no decomposition, or a modifier_noun compound owing a genus atom, is not addressed — the parse keeps the unsplit symbol yet still emits (Inheritance nightmoth moth).
review_run1.notes: The silken_thread fusion with both its genus and its material-adjective atom, the bare class symbol for the non-specific plural object, and the 0.9/0.9 empirical-generic truth value all follow the instruction set.

fields.sentence: If a nightmoth rests on a lantern, the nightmoth sheds silken threads onto the lantern.

review_run1.notes: Indicative conditional correctly becomes a plain Implication with the antecedent's indefinites as premise variables and the consequent's definite "the lantern" bound back to $y (donkey anaphora); the postural "rests on" correctly mints no event and takes the entity-attached (On $x $y) form, and "onto the lantern" is a motion-result Goal with no Result atom. "Silken threads" as a per-binding Skolem group with the fusing material-adjective classifier in the GroupOf kind slot plus its two decomposition atoms follows the plural-classifier rule; Theme for the shed threads is the licensed default when the change test is unclear.

fields.sentence: Silken threads come from the undersides of nightmoths.

q1_issues.issue: (PartOf (sk_underside $x) nightmoth) puts the bare kind nightmoth in PartOf's whole slot instead of minting a per-thread moth witness, so each underside is asserted to be part of the kind rather than of a moth.

q2_gaps: kind-level part-whole inside a generic ('the undersides of nightmoths') — PartOf is defined only over an object's component or a group's member, and a generic definite plural has no group/witness treatment (the determiner rule assumes definite = specific)
review_run1.notes: Compound handling (silken_thread genus plus the material-adjective modifier genus), the bare-plural verbal generic as a distributing rule at 0.9/0.9, and Source for 'from' are all correct. Patient on the intransitive subject is defensible as a non-volitional process.
